newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: TRI unveils 5-yr plan to beat competition.
newsitem.headline: TRI unveils 5-yr plan to beat competition.

text.p: Malaysia's Technology Resources Industries Bhd (TRI) has unveiled a five-year plan to prepare itself for stiffer competition from other telecom firms, the national Bernama news agency reported on Saturday.

The first phase of the plan involves a restructuring, to be carried out within the next 12 to 18 months, where TRI will be split into seven divisions, Tajudin Ramli, chairman and chief executive of the telecommunications group was quoted saying.

The divisions would be mobile services, international services, multimedia and value added services, fixed network, satellite and other transmission, micro and data services, and finally international ventures.
Each of the divisions would be headed by a president, said Tajudin.

He said Cellular Communications Network Sdn Bhd (Celcom), Malaysia's largest cellular phone service and TRI's biggest subsidiary, would also become a "smaller company" towards the end of the five-year plan.
"This is not to say that Celcom is not growing, but others will grow much faster," Tajudin said.
Celcom currently makes up about 65 percent of TRI's earnings, but is only estimated to contribute about 33 percent by the year 2000, Tajudin said.
He also dismissed speculation of TRI buying rival Syarikat Telefon Wireless Sdn Bhd and or that the departure of former Celcom president Rosli Man to that company could affect TRI.
"We lost one president and we get seven more," he quipped.
